July 6, 2026

1st Conference on Free Software and Open AI (seLIA)

When I defended my thesis, WebBuilder, my professors invited me to take part in the 1st Conference on Free Software and Open AI (seLIA), on the URJC Fuenlabrada campus. I submitted my proposal to the organizers and it was received better than I expected, with a lot of interest in the project. The conference brought together 38 talks and workshops spread across several rooms throughout the day, so I got to attend sessions on very different topics: from deploying local AI models without relying on external providers, to debates on how to regulate free software, to the risks of the unchecked productivity of vibe coding. I had given presentations before, but this one felt different. It felt like the audience recognising an effort that usually goes unseen, and it put a fitting close to a stage of my life that was hard but also beautiful, one I look back on with very good memories.
